    AI Overview
    Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged investment accounts for U.S. children under 18, created by the "One Big Beautiful Bill Act". Children born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028, receive a $1,000 government seed deposit. Parents can open accounts via IRS Form 4547 or at TrumpAccounts.gov, with 5 million already registered as of April 2026. 
    Key Features of Trump Accounts: 
    • Funding: $1,000 pilot contribution for 2025–2028 births.
    • Contributions: Parents, relatives, or employers can contribute up to $5,000 annually.
    • Investments: Funds are invested in ETFs/mutual funds, typically tracking the S&P 500.
    • Withdrawals: Funds grow tax-deferred and are locked until the child turns 18.
    • Conversion: At age 18, the account converts to a traditional IRA. 
    How to Participate 
    • Eligibility: Children must have a Social Security number.
    • Opening: Accounts can be established on TrumpAccounts.gov or by filing IRS Form 4547.
    • Launch Date: Contributions begin July 4, 2026. 
    Further Exploration 
    • Read about the $6.25 billion in additional private funding and program details in this article from Chase.
    • View a detailed analysis of the investment and tax implications from Charles Schwab.
    • Explore a report on the technology partners, including Robinhood and BNY, from CNBC. 
    For more information, visit the official Trump Accounts website.

    How to get the $1000 Trump account?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    To get the $1,000 Trump Account contribution, you must enroll eligible children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, using IRS Form 4547. The child must be a U.S. citizen with a Social Security number. The $1,000 "seed money" is deposited by the U.S. Treasury, with accounts opening via trumpaccounts.gov starting July 4, 2026. 
    Eligibility for the $1,000 
    • Birth Date: Child must be born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028.
    • Citizenship: Child must be a U.S. citizen with a valid Social Security number.
    • Role: Parents or legal guardians must make the election. 
    How to Apply 
    1. IRS Form 4547: File Form 4547, "Trump Account Election(s)," with your 2025 tax return or as a standalone submission.
    2. Online Portal: Use the official trumpaccounts.gov website (launching mid-2026) to make the election.
    3. Activation: After election, the Treasury or its agent will provide instructions to activate the account. 
    Key Account Details 
    • No Cost: There is no cost to set up the account, and no contributions are required to receive the $1,000.
    • Contribution Limit: You can add up to $5,000 per year (post-tax) for the child, which grows tax-free.
    • Employer Match: Employers or nonprofits can contribute up to $2,500 per year, which counts toward the $5,000 limit.
    • Older Children: Children born before 2025 can have an account opened, but they are not eligible for the $1,000 pilot contribution.
    • Access: Parents are the custodians until the child turns 18.
